chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Mūsā ibn ʿImrān, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from some of our companions, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
"If a man has a flowing wound, and some of his blood gets onto his garment, then he does not wash it until it heals and the blood stops."

Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: Likewise is the ruling of the garment when the blood of fleas and bedbugs gets onto it, for there is no hardship upon a person in praying in it, even if a large amount of that has affected it.

So the previously mentioned verse indicates that, in the manner we have explained: that Allah the Exalted mentioned that He has lifted hardship from the morally responsible. And we know that the blood of fleas is among that from which it is not possible to guard oneself; if He had obligated the morally responsible person to remove it, hardship would result from that and fulfilling it would become constricted for him. Perhaps that would not even be completed for him, because he cannot be sure that whenever he washes the garment and returns to wearing it, blood will not get on it, so he would remain in this state forever, in difficulty and hardship, and the performance of the obligation would not become easy for him. This is also indicated by it.

key_terms.الْبَرَاغِيثِ: fleas, whose blood stains are difficult to avoid
key_terms.الْبَقِّ: bedbugs, whose blood stains are treated similarly here
key_terms.الْحَرَجَ: undue hardship or constriction removed by divine law
key_terms.الْفَرْضِ: the obligatory act, here referring to salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْمُكَلَّفِينَ: those who are legally and morally responsible before Allah
key_terms.جُرْحٌ سَائِلٌ: a wound that continues to flow with blood
key_terms.دَمِهِ: his blood, meaning blood issuing from the person's own wound

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray in clothes stained with blood from a wound or from fleas and bedbugs?
ai.summary: This passage gives a legal ruling that blood from a continuously flowing wound on one's garment is excused until the wound heals and the bleeding stops. It also extends the ruling to blood from fleas and bedbugs, arguing from the Quranic principle that Allah has lifted hardship from the morally responsible, since avoiding such blood completely is difficult.
